To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size of photosynthetic units in the purple sulfur bacterium Alc. minutisimum depends on light intensity, temperature, and the ratio of light energy to PSU size is maximal at the temperature of ∼15°C

the ratio of light intensities to PSU size in Alc. minutismimum is typical of phototropic organisms in a narrow temperature range (14–17°C), and at extreme temperatures (12 and over 35 °C) the dependence of PSU size on light intensity is different.
